thought
*   **Intro (30s):** "I once had a client tell me, 'We don't need fancy tools, we just need things to work.' It sounds simple, but when you're delegating logic to an agent, 'simple' can turn into a headache if you aren't watching the fine print."
*   **The Scenario (1m):** "I decided to put my coding agent to the test. I gave it a high-level goal: 'Build a functional store locator for a retail brand.' I didn't specify the data source; I wanted to see if it would choose a reliable, industry-standard API on its own."
*   **The Demo/The Error (2m):** [Show screen/code] "Watch the execution here. The agent starts scaffolding the frontend, building the search bar, and setting up the map component. It looks perfect. But then, look at the integration layer. Instead of pulling from a verified provider like Google Maps or Mapbox, it's hitting an obscure, undocumented API it found in a repository. It's essentially trying to build a skyscraper on a foundation of sand. The agent 'thinks' it's succeeded because the code compiles, but the data source is a ticking time bomb."
*   **The Lesson (1m):** "Here's the takeaway: Autonomy requires oversight. An agent can scale your productivity, but it can't replace your judgment. If you let an agent make architectural decisions without setting guardrails on the data and the dependencies, you're not building a solution—you're just automating a future crisis."
*   **Outro (30s):** "The goal isn't to avoid agents; it's to pilot them. Watch the results, but more importantly, watch the logic behind them. Thanks."
